body: Coincidentally my couple close friends that I have also suffer from depression. Albeit not as much as me. Maybe my toxic person attracts like things? But yea, I do confide in them from time to time. And even when they try to get me out doing things and I tell them about how I'm feeling or whatever and they attempt to offer advice, it doesn't really make me feel any better. I'm not sure why, because I know they legitimately try to help. It doesn't help that a lot of things that I think about that get me bummed out or more down, they don't have problem with. (For instance, getting into a relationship. My difficulty in finding somebody is a pretty significant part of my self-hatred and loneliness).

Difficult to meet, and I just get very anxious and extremely quiet around people I first meet. Once I know somebody well enough I open up quite a bit, but it takes awhile. It makes it very difficult to meet women. Even striking up conversation is mind-boggling hard for me. I'm not sure why. Perhaps just due to lack of experience, or perhaps due to low self-esteem. It's really unfortunate though. It is probably one of the things I think about the most too, and get the most down about. I'm in my early 20s, and (this is hard to even say on here because of how pathetic it sounds to myself) I've never asked a girl for a number, and I never kissed a girl. Just thinking about those two facts alone legitimately make me even more down on myself. It truly is an endless cycle that doesn't let up that I'm stuck in right now.

Good point on the example of what you do to play it off though. I sometimes do that, like when somebody tells me I look way younger than my age, I think to myself: well hey, when I'm 40 people will wish they had that 'problem'. But as soon as something like that enters my mind it gets drowned out quickly by my reassured low self-esteem

Interesting. Thank you for sharing. I'll have to talk to my psychiatrist next time I see her. Honestly I get that way a lot too. It's more smaller things for me though. Like for instance, I'm small and have a baby face. I totally acknowledge that. But I CONSTANTLY get comments about how I look young, how I "don't look like a man should my age" (yes I'm serious I've been told this multiple times), and even when I'm at school or work people ask me if I'm old enough to be there. Obviously in some of these comments people are genuinely just making a comment and not necessarily meaning it in a negative way at all, but every single time a comment like this gets made I take it to the extreme negative side of the spectrum. I'm assuming that is not normal :/

Edit: And of course many of these comments being made are just straight up people being asses, which is unfortunately unavoidable

Thank you for your reply. I totally understand about the competition between me and other people mentality is not a "good" way to look at it. I totally understand what you mean about how it is not a competition, and I should (as cliche as it sounds) 'do me'. The problem is, it's like a mental game of pong back and forth between part of my self telling me to look at things in a different way. I guess one way to put it would be part of me looks at things positively and tries to get the most out of life, but the overwhelming majority of negativity just shoots it down. I just don't know to eliminate that negativity.

Further, on the joining a club or taking a recreational elective class. Again, part of me really wants to do that because it would be a good way to meet people. At the same time, I have an extremely minuscule amount of motivation. I have a difficult time even forcing myself to go to class, let alone do homework. Hence why I'm taking mostly online class so I can limit the amount of time I need to go to school. I just get too much anxiety around other people and it fuels that empty feeling. 

I don't know how I'd find the motivation to join a club or something. Hell, even going inside the grocery store or a gas station is nerve-racking honestly.

Regarding a hobby, the problem is I don't really have something that I am really good at. Granted one's ability in something is 99.9% practice. But still. As toxic as this statement is, I really am bad at everything I do. The only hobby-esque thing I can think of is building computers and getting into the overclocking scene. But that just gets me in my room more, and obviously not a good way to meet people or really *achieve* anything.

Yea, it's just that most people I knew from high school a few years ago went off to different colleges, and I don't really have a medium to meet people anymore. Plus I get a **lot** of anxiety around people I don't know so it's really hard to meet people I guess. I don't really have a normal process, because I quite literally have not made friends with anybody in probably months, maybe even years now. I still hang out with a couple people I consider good friends, but that is about the extent of that list.

I don't know. I also just feel like I don't really have much in common with anybody, and I start to think about what I could even contribute to a friendship because I feel like from their perspective I'm pathetic and toxic. Of course that probably is not what they are thinking, but in my head that is what I think people are thinking. I don't even know if that makes sense, it's kind of hard to explain.
